en: On Saturday morning, Maya walked to the small library beside the river. She carried a notebook and a bag of oranges. The librarian greeted her warmly and showed her a table near the window.

Several neighbors were already waiting there. They wanted to plan a garden behind the building, where an empty patch of ground had collected leaves all winter. Maya opened her notebook and asked everyone what they hoped to grow. One child suggested strawberries.

An older man preferred beans because they could climb a wooden frame. Another neighbor offered to bring flowers that would attract bees. Before choosing anything, the group went outside to check how much sunlight reached the ground. They measured the space with a piece of string and drew a simple map. Then they divided the work into small jobs.

Over the following weeks, the neighbors returned with tools, seeds, and buckets of water. Some days it rained, so they stayed inside and made labels for the plants. Nobody expected the garden to be perfect. They simply wanted a place where people could meet and learn from one another. By early summer, green shoots covered the soil. Maya sat on a bench with her notebook and watched the children count the first strawberries. At the bottom of the page, she wrote that the next meeting would begin after lunch.

Daniel arrived at the railway station before sunrise. His train would leave in half an hour, giving him enough time to buy breakfast. He chose a warm roll and found a quiet seat near the departure board.

The journey would take him through the mountains to visit his sister. She had recently moved into an apartment above a bakery and promised to show him around the neighborhood. Daniel checked his ticket, put his phone away, and listened for the announcement.

When the train arrived, he helped a passenger lift a heavy suitcase onto the luggage rack. His seat faced a wide window. Soon the city streets disappeared, replaced by fields and narrow streams. At the first stop, a family joined the carriage carrying a large picnic basket. Their youngest child asked whether the mountains would have snow on top.

Daniel looked outside and said they would find out together. As the train climbed higher, the fields gave way to dark trees and rocky slopes. A few white patches remained in the shade, even though the valley was already warm. He took a photograph to send to his sister, then returned to his book. By noon, the train was slowing beside a small platform decorated with flower pots. His sister waved from the entrance. They walked toward the bakery, talking about lunch and the places they would explore the next day.

The museum opened a new room dedicated to everyday inventions. Visitors could examine old lamps, clocks, and kitchen tools. Near the entrance, a guide invited a group of students to guess how each object had been used.

One student picked up a wooden model of a water wheel. The guide explained how moving water could turn the wheel and power a machine. Instead of giving a long lecture, she asked the students to pour water through a small demonstration channel.

The wheel began to spin, and a tiny hammer moved up and down. Everyone stepped closer to see the connection between the parts. Next, they tried a hand operated printing press. Each student arranged a few letters, spread ink across the surface, and pressed a sheet of paper against the type. Their first attempts were uneven, but the words were readable.

At the final table, the students designed inventions of their own. One drew a lamp that could be repaired without special tools. Another imagined a watering system for people who traveled often. The guide asked them to describe the problem before explaining the solution. This made their drawings simpler and more useful. Before leaving, they placed their ideas on a board beside the door. The teacher photographed the board and promised that they would build a few models in class. Outside, the afternoon sunlight made the printed pages look brighter.
zh: 星期六早上，小芸走進河邊的圖書館，準備參加社區的花園討論會。她帶著一本筆記和幾顆橘子，館員請她坐在靠窗的長桌旁，先喝一杯溫水。
幾位鄰居陸續到齊，大家想把館後的空地整理成小花園。有人希望種草莓，有人想種豆子，也有人願意提供吸引蜜蜂的花苗。
小芸把每個人的想法記下來，再請大家一起到外面看看陽光和土壤的情況。他們用繩子量出空地的範圍，在紙上畫了一張簡單的地圖。靠牆的位置適合放工具，中央可以留下走道，讓推輪椅的人也能輕鬆通過。

討論結束前，大家分配了工作，有人負責準備種子，有人負責借工具，還有人答應每天下班後來澆水。孩子們則想替每一種植物畫上自己的名牌。接下來的幾個星期，鄰居們帶著鏟子和水桶陸續回來。有時下雨，大家就留在室內製作標籤，順便交換種植的經驗。他們並不要求花園立刻變得漂亮，只希望這裡能讓不同年紀的人一起學習。到了初夏，土裡冒出一排排嫩芽，第一顆草莓也慢慢轉紅。小芸坐在長椅上，看著孩子仔細數著葉片，在筆記最後寫下下次聚會的時間。離開之前，她把剩下的橘子分給大家，約好下個週末再來整理走道。
天還沒亮，明哲就到了火車站。他要搭車去山城探望妹妹，距離發車還有半個小時。他買了一份熱早餐，坐在候車室裡，慢慢看著牆上的路線圖。
妹妹剛搬進麵包店樓上的公寓，說附近有一條安靜的步道，很適合下午散步。明哲確認車票之後，把手機收進背包，專心聽著廣播。
月台上的燈還亮著，遠處已經傳來列車接近的聲音，旅客開始排隊上車。找到座位後，他先幫旁邊的乘客把行李放好，再轉頭看向窗外。城市的街道漸漸變成田野，細小的溪流沿著鐵道延伸。

第一站有一家人上車，帶著裝滿點心的提籃。小女孩問山頂還有沒有積雪，明哲笑著說，等火車爬得更高，大家就可以一起找找看。車廂裡的氣氛因此輕鬆起來。不久之後，窗外出現大片樹林和灰色的岩壁，背光的山坡上果然留著幾片白雪。明哲拍了一張照片傳給妹妹，然後繼續讀背包裡的書。接近中午，列車在擺滿花盆的小月台停下。妹妹站在出口揮手，兩人沿著石板路走向麵包店，商量午餐要吃什麼。她說最近發現一家賣熱湯的小店，老闆每天都用不同的蔬菜。明哲聽了很期待，決定先放好行李，再一起慢慢走過去，享受這個不用趕時間的下午。
博物館新開了一間介紹日常發明的展覽室，裡面擺著舊燈具、時鐘和廚房工具。導覽員請學生先觀察每件物品，再猜猜它們過去的用途，大家都很期待。
一位學生拿起木製水車的模型，問水流怎麼能讓機器工作。導覽員沒有立刻講解，而是請他把水倒進旁邊的小水道。
水車轉動起來，連接的木槌也跟著上下移動，其他學生立刻靠近，仔細看清楚每個零件的關係。接著，他們試著操作手動印刷機。每個人先排好幾個字，再把油墨輕輕塗在表面，最後將紙張壓上去。

第一次印出的字有些歪斜，但仍然看得清楚。老師提醒大家，好的工具需要反覆調整，使用的人也要練習。他們於是重新排列字塊，這次放慢速度，終於印出一張整齊的小卡片。最後一張桌子留給學生設計自己的發明。有人想畫一盞容易修理的檯燈，也有人希望做出能自動澆水的裝置。導覽員請他們先說明遇到的問題，再介紹解決的方法。這樣討論之後，原本複雜的圖案變得簡單，也更接近實際需要。離開前，學生把作品貼在門邊的展示板上，老師拍照留下紀錄，答應下週在教室裡做幾個模型。走出博物館時，午後的陽光照在小卡片上，每個人都小心地把自己的作品收進書包。
